question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched regarding the major military victories of the English East India Company and their commanders? [EIC Commanders and Battles]
options: Battle of Seringapatam (1799): Arthur Wellesley (later Duke of Wellington) as the supreme Commander-in-Chief of all EIC forces
wrong_fact: Arthur Wellesley served as a division commander and later governor of Mysore after the battle, but the overall Commander-in-Chief of the British forces during the Siege and Battle of Seringapatam in 1799 was General George Harris.
explanation: The military organization of the British was characterized by professional leadership. Robert Clive won at Plassey. Hector Munro commanded the EIC coalition at Buxar. Sir Eyre Coote defeated the French under Lally at Wandiwash. At Seringapatam, General George Harris commanded the victorious forces, while Arthur Wellesley served under him.

question: The British EIC organized its army into three separate presidency armies. Which of the following matches linking a presidency army to its geographical recruitment patterns or characteristics is NOT correct? [Presidency Armies and Recruitment]
options: Bengal Army: Recruited heavily from high-caste Hindu (Bhumihar, Rajput) and Muslim peasant-soldiers of Awadh and Bihar
Madras Army: Recruited from a more diverse pool of lower-caste groups, Muslims, and native Christians of southern India
Bombay Army: Recruited largely from the Marathas and local Konkan castes, as well as recruits from Uttar Pradesh
Punjab Frontier Force: Formed in 1849 as an elite cavalry unit composed entirely of British-born soldiers stationed in Lahore
wrong_fact: The Punjab Frontier Force (or Piffer force) was raised in 1849 and was composed of native Punjabi, Sikh, Pathan, and Gurkha soldiers under British officers, not entirely of British-born soldiers.
explanation: The military organization of the EIC relied on native recruits (sepoys) led by British officers. The Bengal Army preferred high-caste recruits from Awadh and Bihar. The Madras and Bombay armies recruited from more heterogeneous populations, which made them less prone to caste-based mutinies. The Punjab Frontier Force was raised after the annexation of Punjab in 1849, recruiting local frontier tribesmen and Punjabis to police the border.

question: The EIC standard military organization relied on advanced tactical deployments, weapons, and training. Which of the following matches between a military unit or doctrine and its geographical introduction/impact is NOT correct? [Military Technology and Tactics]
options: Shrapnel Shells: First deployed by the EIC artillery at the Battle of Assaye (1803) in the Deccan to defeat Maratha batteries
Congreve Rockets: Copied from Tipu Sultan's Mysore rockets and manufactured by the British at Woolwich Arsenal for global use
Flintlock Musket (Brown Bess): Standardized infantry weapon of the EIC line infantry, replacing the slower matchlock muskets used by Indian rulers
Regimental System: Introduced by the French under Joseph François Dupleix at Pondicherry, which the British copied and standardized across India
wrong_fact: Shrapnel shells were not deployed at the Battle of Assaye in September 1803. The battle was won by Wellesley's rapid infantry and cavalry charges and capturing Maratha artillery; shrapnel shells were first used by the British in 1804 in Surinam.
explanation: The military superiority of the British was rooted in tactical standardization. They adopted the regimental system (originally initiated in India by Dupleix with French sepoys). The standard issue weapon was the flintlock 'Brown Bess' musket, which could be fired much faster and was more reliable than the matchlocks used by many Indian states. The Congreve rockets were directly inspired by the iron-cased Mysore rockets used by Hyder Ali and Tipu Sultan at Pollilur and Seringapatam.
